title: Olivia and the Floating Rock
subtitle: Water can hold you up
author: Olivia's Shelf
blurb: Olivia drops a pebble and a wooden boat, then learns that water hugs upward — and that is why some things float.

magic.launch: The little rocket pushed the air, and the air pushed back.
magic.drop: Everything falls. That pull has a name: gravity.

openai.instructions: Warm, clear storyteller reading a science picture book to a child. Curious, never lecturing. Pause at full stops.

pages.heading: Sink and float
pages.text: {Olivia} dropped a {pebble}. It sank. She dropped a wooden {boat}. It floated on the {workshop} tray.

pages.heading: An upward hug
pages.text: "Water pushes {up} on everything in it," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "That upward hug is called {buoyancy}."

pages.heading: Heavier than the hug
pages.text: "A thing {sinks} if it is heavier than the water it pushes aside," said Elon. The pebble was. The boat was not.

pages.heading: A boat is mostly air
pages.text: "A boat is mostly empty {air}," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "It pushes aside a lot of water, so the water hugs it {up}."

pages.heading: Salty hugs harder
pages.text: They added salt. The boat sat a little {higher}. "Salt water hugs a little {harder}," said Elon. "The sea is like that."

pages.heading: Keep asking why
pages.text: "Why does ice float?" asked {Olivia:olivia/ask}. "Ice takes more space than the same water," said {Elon:elon/teach}. "Ask why again tomorrow."

end.heading: The End
end.text: Water hugs upward. If the hug is stronger than the weight, the thing floats.
end.prompt: What would you try in a tub of water tomorrow?

credits: Painted for Olivia's Shelf. Elon is a picture-book inventor who teaches physics; this is not a biography.

questions.right: Yes! Water pushes up on everything in it.
questions.wrong: Elon called it an upward hug. Buoyancy.

options.label: when it is heavier than the water it pushes aside

questions.right: That's right. Heavier than its water-space, it sinks.
questions.wrong: It sinks if it outweighs the water it pushes aside.

questions.right: Yes. Lots of air means lots of water pushed aside.
questions.wrong: A boat is mostly empty air.
